children.text: Our influencers are Mark Rober, a former NASA engineer, and Lindsay Nikole, a zoology graduate. Both are education influencers whose videos rely on “edutainment,” making educational material fun and exciting, rather than resembling a school lecture. They must account for the affordances and constraints of the platform, working within algorithms, ensuring their content is relevant and within platform rules, all while remaining attentive to viewers’ attention spans. Edutainment influencers subtly use the rhetorical appeal ethos to build credibility in the background of their content. Rober does not need to constantly remind his audience of his experience as a NASA engineer, just as Nikole does not need to repeatedly emphasize her background in wildlife conservation. Their expertise is demonstrated throughout their content, with their credentials remaining available to curious viewers. Edutainment influencers balance pathos carefully with their ethos. Although both Rober and Nikole have zany personalities and content, neither becomes so “clownish” that their credibility is undermined. These appeals support the logos at the educational core of the video. As influencers compete for their viewers’ attention, educators on entertainment platforms must communicate differently. If content is not immediately engaging, viewers may scroll past it. Edutainment addresses this by putting complex ideas into engaging formats, making learning feel more like something to actively seek out.

Mark Rober is an American engineer and youtuber who formerly worked at NASA in their Jet Propulsion laboratory for nine years. He spent seven of those years working on the Curiosity Mars Rover, and then worked in Apple’s Special Projects Group until 2020 to become a full time youtuber. He is known for his hilarious videos where he makes do it yourself gadgets and other projects that bring in aspects of both engineering and science in a fun way for all ages. His channel, started in 2011, features insane experiments such as glitter bombs for package thieves and obstacle courses for squirrels. He has amassed over 80 million subscribers throughout the course of his channel. In 2022, he launched CrunchLabs, a STEM subscription box company. Alongside Mr. Beast, he led the #TeamWater campaign which generated over 40 million dollars for clean water access. In 2026, Rober was named to TIME’s list of top creators.
The Most Mysterious Squid (That We Know Of) | Lindsay Nikole

Lindsay Nikole is a zoologist who has experience working with several wildlife and animal sanctuaries, as well as a B.S. in Zoology from Oregon State University. Her content focuses on zoology, paleontology, and evolution. Nikole produces content on several platforms, including YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, and Patreon. Across all of these platforms, Nikole balances a conversational and humorous tone with well-researched and, at-times, dense scientific material. In this, she creates “edutainment.” Her teaching method is bolstered by her comedy and irreverence, making potentially intimidating natural science accessible. The description of an influencer fits Nikole, but many may characterize her as a science communicator. Her content has a distinct internet style, seen in her profanity, memes, slang, and often-exaggerated reactions, while still being informative. Her intended audience is a diverse crowd, from PhD zoologists to people with little formal science education, and Nikole attempts to make them laugh so hard they do not realize they are learning until it is too late. Nikole persuades this broad audience by combining scientific credibility with humor and internet imagery, making specialized knowledge feel accessible.
